basics.name: Tom Lamb
basics.label: DPhil Candidate in Machine Learning
basics.summary: DPhil candidate in machine learning at the Torr Vision Group, University of Oxford. Research interests in AI safety: eliciting, producing, and giving guarantees for the safe and reliable deployment of ML models, specifically LLMs and reasoning models.

work.name: University of Oxford
work.summary: Research intern funded by Google DeepMind and supervised by Francisco Girbal Eiras and Prof. Philip H. S. Torr. Introduced a faithful-imitation framework for teacher-student networks, formulated LP-based upper/lower bounds on measures of local confidence disagreement between teacher and student models, and designed a distillation method yielding verifiably more calibrated student models. Led to the paper 'Faithful Knowledge Distillation'.

work.name: University of Durham
work.summary: Collaborated with Prof. Herbert Gangl to conjecture and prove new identities relating polylogarithmic integrals over the unit square to linear combinations of multiple zeta values.

education.summary: Supervised by Prof. Philip H.S. Torr (University of Oxford) and Dr. Tim G.J. Rudner (NYU). Published at top-tier ML conferences including ICML, NeurIPS and ICLR. Research on: semantic calibration and uncertainty quantification for LLMs; steering LLMs adaptively at inference time; biases in VLMs; and universal in-context approximation of fully recurrent models including SSMs.

Courses: Reinforcement Learning, Bayesian Statistics and MCMC Methods, Probabilistic Modeling and Reasoning, Natural Language Understanding, Generation and Machine Translation. MSc dissertation: 'Self-Supervised Learning of Tractable Generative Models', supervised by Dr. Antonio Vergari. Applied conditional composite log-likelihood estimation (CCLE) with novel patching schemes to train EiNet models.

education.score: John Crowther and Percy Heywood Prizes
education.summary: Specialised in pure mathematics. Courses: Algebraic Topology, Riemannian Geometry, Representation Theory, Partial Differential Equations, Algebraic Number Theory, Galois Theory. MMath dissertation: 'An Introduction to Modular Forms and the Eichler-Shimura Isomorphism', supervised by Prof. Herbert Gangl.
